subject: Mixed Pareto and Normal Stan model not working

messages.author: 778746842555fe22
messages.subject: Mixed Pareto and Normal Stan model not working
parts:
I'm trying to learn Stan via rstan (since I'm familiar with R). I've tried running a simple mixed Pareto and Normal model. It compiles fine (as far as I can tell), but it fails to sample, giving me the error:

"Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : 

  c++ exception (unknown reason)

error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done."

My R+rstan code is below:

library(rstan)
rpareto = function(n, location, shape){location/runif(n)^(1/shape)}
sdvec=runif(1e1,0.1,1)
HMFtest=list(x=rpareto(1e1,10,2)+rnorm(1e1,0,sdvec), sdev=sdvec, N=1e1)

HMF.stan <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  real x[N];
  real sdev[N];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0, upper=20> y_min;
  real<lower=0, upper=5> alpha;
  real<lower=y_min> xtrue[N];
}
model {
  y_min ~ lognormal(1, 1) T[0,20];
  alpha ~ lognormal(1, 1) T[0, 5];
  xtrue ~ pareto(y_min, alpha);
  x ~ normal(xtrue, sdev);
}
"

stan.test <- stan(model_code=HMF.stan, data=HMFtest, pars=c('y_min','alpha'), chains=1, iter=30000, warmup=10000)

I've already asked a similar question on stackoverflow and was given some pointers (it now starts to sample at least), but the sampling still seems to severely misbehave, and the sampling stops when it attempts samples at the limits specified (I could see this when I printed out y_min and alpha). If I change pareto->normal the model works (just with a nonsensical fit). This seems to somehow be a problem with the pareto distribution implementation, or at least with how I'm attempting to use it. To confuse things a bit I can fit a pure pareto model with no trouble, it is when it has an extra normal 'noise' component that things start going wrong.

messages.subject: Re: Mixed Pareto and Normal Stan model not working
parts:
Given Seth's success running on Windows, could somebody who is running Mountain Lion and rstan give the example a try?

I'm thinking it is an issue with my ancient gcc compiler somehow.

A

On Sunday, February 8, 2015 at 4:00:45 PM UTC+8, Aaron Robotham wrote:

I'm trying to learn Stan via rstan (since I'm familiar with R). I've tried running a simple mixed Pareto and Normal model. It compiles fine (as far as I can tell), but it fails to sample, giving me the error:

"Error in sampler$call_sampler(args_list[[i]]) : 

  c++ exception (unknown reason)

error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done."

My R+rstan code is below:

library(rstan)
rpareto = function(n, location, shape){location/runif(n)^(1/shape)}
sdvec=runif(1e1,0.1,1)
HMFtest=list(x=rpareto(1e1,10,2)+rnorm(1e1,0,sdvec), sdev=sdvec, N=1e1)

HMF.stan <- "
data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  real x[N];
  real sdev[N];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0, upper=20> y_min;
  real<lower=0, upper=5> alpha;
  real<lower=y_min> xtrue[N];
}
model {
  y_min ~ lognormal(1, 1) T[0,20];
  alpha ~ lognormal(1, 1) T[0, 5];
  xtrue ~ pareto(y_min, alpha);
  x ~ normal(xtrue, sdev);
}
